messages:
deploy-bot: starting canary rollout v5.2.1 -> traffic split 10% :rocket:
deploy-bot: targets: eu-west1, us-central1. rolling out new runtime with KV-cache tweaks.

sarah: seeing spike in 502/503s on eu-west1 canary nodes, started ~2m after rollout. dashboard -> https://redwood.internal/metrics/rollouts/4087654321 :rotating_light:

mike: logs show repeated errors in runtime kv cache layer: `KVCache: failed to deserialize entry` then immediate 5xx. grabbing stack traces.

mike: paste:
```
2026-03-15T14:12:08Z ERROR runtime.kvcache: key=conv-1234, err=corrupt-length
2026-03-15T14:12:08Z ERROR handler: write response failed status=503 peer=canary-03
```

priya: paging SRE oncall, running quick health check: `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" https://canary-eu.health/ready` -> returns 503 from canary-03.

oncall-sre: paging received. escalating to incident channel and grabbing ownership. canary traffic should be pinned at 10% — we can kill the rollout if needed.

emma: tagging in infra/runtime. if kvcache code path failing on deserialization maybe bad compatibility from new runtime build. recommend abort flag.

oncall-sre: setting feature flag `rollout-v5.2.1` -> OFF (kill-switch). executing: `curl -X POST https://flags.internal/api/flip -d '{"flag":"rollout-v5.2.1","state":false}'`
oncall-sre: done. traffic controller confirms revert to previous version for eu-west1 canary. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: rollout aborted by oncall-sre. traffic rollback initiated. Canary cluster eu-west1 scaling down new pods.

sarah: post-rollback metrics: 5xx rate dropping but still some tail errors from 14:16–14:19. looks like lingering connections to canary nodes.

mike: found root cause: a change in serialization alignment in PR#4829 — old nodes expect little-endian varints, new runtime wrote a length field differently. in most cases it's tolerant but some cached entries become unreadable -> handler returns 500.

priya: mitigation applied: disabled KV cache for canary nodes via runtime flag `--kvcache=off` and restarted canary pool. command used: `kubectl set env deployment/canary -n canary RUNTIME_KVCACHE=false`

mike: after disabling KV cache, error logs for corrupt-length went to zero. health probes green on eu-west1.

oncall-sre: confirming customer impact: estimated ~320 requests failed to hosted-api customers in eu-west1 over 7 minutes. no SLA breach expected but ops to notify top 5 affected customers.

emma: good catch. opening a rollback follow-up ticket: https://redwood.internal/issue/RW-12987 with root cause and action items (revert serialization change, add integration test for cache compatibility).

priya: recommending postmortem include: canary traffic isolation improvement (drain connections faster), pre-rollout cache compatibility check, and an automatic kill-switch when specific kvcache-corrupt counter spikes above threshold.

oncall-sre: handing off to daytime SRE (emma) for follow-up. oncall shift ends in 20m. leaving channel notes and runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kvcache-compat.md

emma: taking over. will coordinate customer comms and patch release. thanks team. :pray:

incident-bot: incident created RW-4087654321, severity: P2, assignees: emma, mike, priya. timeline auto-snapshot attached.

sarah: thumbs — monitoring for 30m and will close thread when no regressions.

mike: quick snippet for postmortem logs collection:
```
# collect corrupt events
jq -r '.events[] | select(.error=="corrupt-length")' /var/log/canary/*.json > /tmp/corrupt-events.json
```

oncall-sre: closing handoff — if anything spikes re-open and we'll abort global rollout. :lock:

sarah: noting to update deployment playbook with explicit `kvcache` toggles and more conservative canary parsing.

emma: created follow-on release v5.2.2 candidate with serialization revert. will run extended canary in staging first.

sarah: thanks all — nice rapid abort and mitigation.
